entry.name: Machine Learning Specialization
entry.note: Andrew Ng's rebuilt classic; the most common starting point in the field

covers: Supervised learning, including linear and logistic regression
Decision trees and tree ensembles such as random forests and boosted trees
Best practices for making models generalize to real-world data
Python tools including NumPy, scikit-learn and TensorFlow
reading.format: Three courses delivered online. Lessons give an intuitive, visual explanation first, then a step-by-step walkthrough in code, with the underlying math in optional videos. The program includes practice quizzes, graded assignments and practice labs.
reading.summary: The Machine Learning Specialization is a beginner-friendly, three-course online program created by DeepLearning.AI and Stanford Online and taught by Andrew Ng. It is a rebuilt and expanded version of Andrew Ng's original machine learning course. Finishing it shows you can build and train machine learning models in Python and apply them to real applications.
reading.audience: It is aimed at people breaking into AI, including those without prior math knowledge or a rigorous coding background. It also suits people who did not finish the original Machine Learning course and those who completed it and want to refresh their foundations.
reading.prerequisites: The program does not require prior math knowledge or a rigorous coding background.
